passages.t: Twenty-four divisions of priests, by lot
passages.happening:
‘These were the divisions of the descendants of Aaron’ (verse 1). Aaron's sons Nadab and Abihu died before their father and had no sons, so the priesthood passed through Eleazar and Ithamar (verse 2). With the help of Zadok, of Eleazar's line, and Ahimelech, of Ithamar's, David divides them by their service: sixteen family heads from Eleazar and eight from Ithamar (verses 3-4). ‘Thus they were divided by lot’ (verse 5), and a Levite scribe records the names before the king, the officers and the family heads (verse 6).

The twenty-four lots fall in order, ‘the seventh to Hakkoz, the eighth to Abijah’ (verse 10) among them (verses 7-18). ‘This was their appointed order for service when they entered the house of the LORD’ (verse 19).
passages.hearers:
After the Levites, the priests: Aaron's descendants, who alone offered sacrifice. The chapter sets up the rotation by which they took turns in the temple. Each division served for a week at a time, as later Jewish sources describe, and all of them together at the great festivals. Who to notice: Zadok and Ahimelech, the two priestly lines of David's day, and Abijah, the eighth lot.

Nadab and Abihu died when they offered unauthorized fire before the LORD, so the priesthood ran through Eleazar and Ithamar. Later Solomon removed Abiathar, of Ithamar's line, and Zadok's line became the leading family in the Jerusalem temple.

Casting lots was a common way of making decisions in Israel, understood as leaving the choice to God. The word, goral, first meant the marked stone, then the share it assigned; the lot had divided the land among the tribes under Joshua, and now it divides the service. It kept the larger line of Eleazar and the smaller line of Ithamar from rivalry and removed favoritism, and the public record made it official.

The divisions lasted for centuries. Nehemiah 12 lists priestly families after the exile, several with names from this chapter. The first division, Jehoiarib, was the family of Mattathias, the priest who began the Maccabean revolt in the second century BC. Many scholars think the chapter reflects the system as it ran in the Chronicler's own day, credited to David as its founder; others take it as an institution of David's continued through later centuries.
passages.later: The eighth division appears at the opening of Luke's Gospel: ‘there was a priest named Zechariah, who belonged to the priestly division of Abijah’ (Luke 1:5). ‘One day while Zechariah’s division was on duty and he was serving as priest before God, he was chosen by lot, according to the custom of the priesthood, to enter the temple of the Lord and burn incense’ (Luke 1:8-9), and there an angel told him of the birth of John the Baptist.
passages.asks: A list that looks like paperwork was still running when the Gospel story began. Ask what faithful, ordinary order in your life God might use long after you have gone. And ask where you need to leave a choice to God rather than to rivalry or favor.

passages.t: The rest of the Levites, by lot as well
passages.happening: A further list names the heads of other Levite families, from Amram, Izhar, Hebron, Uzziel and Merari (verses 20-30). ‘As their brothers the descendants of Aaron did, they also cast lots in the presence of King David and of Zadok, Ahimelech, and the heads of the families of the priests and Levites’ (verse 31), the family heads and their younger brothers alike.
passages.hearers:
This short list partly repeats chapter 23 and carries some families on by a generation. Its point is in the last verse. The Levites, too, received their places by lot, in public, before the king and the priests, and the head of a family drew on the same terms as his younger brother. No rank bought a better place.

Written records of descent mattered greatly in later years. After the exile some families were excluded from the priesthood because they could not find their genealogical records. Lists like this one were how a family knew where it belonged.
passages.later: A proverb says, ‘The lot is cast into the lap, but its every decision is from the LORD’ (Proverbs 16:33).
passages.asks: The family heads and their younger brothers drew lots alike. Ask where you have expected a better place because of age or standing. And ask how your church gives the younger and the less known an equal share in its work.
